why: DMN 1.6 §10.3.2.15: "By definition, FEEL(e1 != e2) is FEEL(not(e 1= e2))", so operands that = cannot compare are the same semantic error for != (§7.3.8: the evaluation "MUST report or log diagnostic information and SHALL return null"): the null carries the = reason, is counted, and fails strict mode; B-FEEL keeps its true and lists the error, as it does for =.
